topic.title: My Notes on Rules & Strategy — What's Your Approach?

messages.content:
Sharing my getting-started notes as a one-page visual summary (in Japanese) — the rules, the constraints that actually shape strategy, and a rough roadmap. Quick gloss of the main points.
• You submit two coupled things: a policy (main.py) + a deck (deck.csv).
• No ingress/egress during episodes → the agent must be self-contained (no live LLM calls).
• The engine hands you the legal moves each turn, so a first working agent is easier than it looks.
• Win/loss TrueSkill, latest 2 subs count → consistency beats blowouts.

How are you approaching it? Net-decking a known Standard list or building from scratch? Heuristics + search, imitation from the exported top episodes, or full self-play RL? What's your approach?

messages.content: how do you export top episodes? do you have to download it one by one manually?
messages.rawMarkdown: how do you export top episodes? do you have to download it one by one manually?

replies.content:
Good question! Not one by one — the organizers are posting a daily export of the top-rated episodes in the forums, and you can pull replays via the Kaggle CLI/MCP rather than the UI (docs: https://github.com/Kaggle/kaggle-cli/blob/main/docs/simulation_competitions.md).

And maybe automating that whole fetch → parse → train loop is itself part of the winning play. Could be a job for an agent too.
